messages.content: I need to set up a two-night Columbus client trip. I can leave Minneapolis Sunday after 3:00 p.m., the kickoff is Monday afternoon, and Tuesday meetings end at 4:00. I need to be home Tuesday night. Air has to stay at or below $650, and the hotel cap is $240 a night before tax. Nothing is booked yet.

What are the dates, and is the office actually at Easton Town Center or just nearby? That distinction matters because an Easton hotel may be walkable, while an airport hotel would mean repeated rides.

Sunday, December 9 through Tuesday, December 11. The office is on Easton Way, about two blocks from the Hilton at Easton. I would fly MSP to CMH. I am trying to decide whether staying by the airport is simpler or whether that only looks simpler.

I’ll compare both arrangements. Two details first: what time does the Monday kickoff begin, and will you have only a carry-on? Those affect how useful a late Sunday flight and a tight Tuesday airport transfer would be.
Kickoff is at 1:00 Monday. Carry-on only. On Tuesday I can leave the office at 4:00, although I should allow ten minutes in case the meeting runs over.

The cleanest flight pairing I found is a Sunday nonstop leaving MSP at 4:45 p.m. and reaching CMH at 7:38 p.m., with a Tuesday nonstop leaving CMH at 6:25 p.m. and reaching MSP at 7:32 p.m. The current round trip is $512. A later Sunday nonstop runs 7:30-10:24 p.m. for $548. Both remain under the airfare ceiling; the fares include a carry-on but no checked bag.
The 4:45 departure is workable. Is there any reason to pay for the later one other than having more of Sunday at home?

No operational advantage. The 4:45 flight gets you to either hotel before roughly 8:30 p.m., leaves time for dinner, and gives more recovery room if the flight slips. The later flight likely puts you in the room near 11:00 p.m. The $36 premium buys only the later departure from Minneapolis.
Use the 4:45 option for the comparison. What hotel choices fit? I do not need anything elaborate for this trip.

Near the client, the Hilton Columbus at Easton is showing $229 per night before tax, and a second Easton option about a mile away is $208. Near CMH, two hotels with airport shuttles are showing $174 and $189. All four fit the nightly cap. The Hilton at Easton is the only one of these that makes the office a straightforward two-block walk.
Put actual transportation numbers around that. Assume rideshare rather than renting a car.

For the Hilton at Easton, estimate $20-$28 from CMH Sunday and the same range back Tuesday. Monday and Tuesday office trips can be walked, so projected local transportation is $40-$56 total. For an airport hotel, the hotel shuttle should cover Sunday arrival and the Tuesday hotel-to-airport leg. You would still need airport-area hotel to Easton and back Monday, then hotel to Easton Tuesday and Easton to CMH after the meeting. At roughly $18-$26 per ride, that is $72-$104 total. Surge pricing could push either estimate higher.
Small correction: Tuesday I would check out in the morning and take my bag to the office. So there would not be a hotel-to-airport shuttle that afternoon.

That removes one transfer but not one paid ride. The airport-hotel sequence becomes shuttle from CMH Sunday, rides hotel-office and office-hotel Monday, then hotel-office Tuesday and office-CMH after the meeting. That remains four rides, about $72-$104. At Easton, it is one ride from CMH Sunday, two nights in the same place, a short walk to the office both days, and one ride to CMH Tuesday.
How safe is the 6:25 flight if the meeting ends at 4:00 but could go to 4:10?

Reasonable, provided you leave directly. Easton to CMH is commonly about 10-20 minutes by car, but I would budget 30 minutes for pickup and traffic. A 4:10 departure should put you at the terminal around 4:40, about 1 hour 45 minutes before takeoff. With a carry-on and mobile boarding pass, that is a comfortable target. A major traffic incident or a meeting extending well past 4:30 would erode it.
There is also a cheaper return with a connection, correct? I saw something around 7:00.

Yes. A one-stop return leaves CMH at 7:10 p.m. and reaches MSP at 11:02 p.m.; paired with the 4:45 Sunday outbound, it is $426 round trip. It gives you 45 more minutes before departure but adds a connection, arrives about three and a half hours later, and saves $86. The 6:25 nonstop is the stronger fit for getting home Tuesday night without turning the return into a long evening.
Agreed. Compare the total for the Hilton at Easton against the cheaper airport hotel, including estimated hotel tax and rides.

Using the $512 nonstop airfare: Hilton at Easton is $458 for two nights before tax. With roughly $80 in hotel tax and $48 as the midpoint rideshare estimate, the trip is about $1,098. The $174 airport hotel is $348 before tax; with about $61 tax and $88 in midpoint rides, the estimate is about $1,009. The airport plan is approximately $89 cheaper overall, but it requires four office-related rides and more coordination.
The Easton total is acceptable. Is there a less expensive Easton property that stays simple, or does the extra distance give back the room savings?

The $208 Easton property saves $42 before tax over two nights, but it is about a mile from the office. In December, planning to walk with a work bag is less dependable, and even two short rides would consume much of the savings. Its estimated total is about $1,075 if you walk and roughly $1,095-$1,110 if you use rides locally. It does not materially improve the trip over the Hilton.
Then make the Hilton at Easton and the two nonstops the working choice. Give me the schedule and what still needs confirmation, but do not treat anything as booked.

Working itinerary, not booked: Sunday, December 9, depart MSP at 4:45 p.m. and arrive CMH at 7:38 p.m.; take a rideshare to the Hilton Columbus at Easton and check in for two nights at the quoted $229 nightly rate before tax. Monday, walk the two blocks to the 1:00 p.m. kickoff and return to the same hotel. Tuesday, check out in the morning, take your carry-on to the office, leave immediately when meetings end at 4:00-4:10 p.m., and rideshare to CMH. Depart nonstop at 6:25 p.m. and arrive MSP at 7:32 p.m. Estimated trip total is $1,098: $512 airfare, $458 room charge, about $80 hotel tax, and about $48 for rides. Before purchase, recheck the exact flight times and fare, hotel availability and cancellation deadline, the final taxed room total, and the rideshare pickup plan at the office. No flight, hotel, or ground transportation reservation has been made.
